summary: This bill expands the advanced reactor demonstration program to prioritize testing and developing fourth-generation nuclear reactors, small modular reactors, and specialized micro-reactors at a minimum of 10 different sites, including those not owned by the Department of Energy, and encourages cost-sharing partnerships with private industry.

scores.thoughts: The bill expands the scope of an existing advanced reactor demonstration program, requiring the testing and development of various nuclear reactor designs on at least 10 different sites. This expansion of activities, even with a call for cost-sharing, implies an increase in government expenditure for research, development, and demonstration projects related to nuclear energy.

The bill promotes the development and deployment of advanced nuclear reactors, including fourth-generation, small modular, and micro-reactors. Nuclear energy is a carbon-free power source, and its expansion is generally considered a measure to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and protect the environment from climate change impacts.
